elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "TrueLink shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client and its affiliates..." — express defence duty running to Client and affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...indemnify and hold harmless Client and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)..."

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (i): "an allegation that the Interface, Hosting Services or Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — tracks the defined deliverables/services of this Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (iii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or Credit Data caused by TrueLink".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (iv): "TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Each indemnity under this Section 12 is conditioned on the indemnified party giving prompt written notice of the claim..."

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "...the indemnifying party having control of the defense of the claim..." — control is expressly allocated to the indemnifying party.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "...the indemnified party providing reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense."

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 12(a) as rewritten now reads only "(i) any claim arising out of or relating to Client Content provided by Client, and (ii) any violation by Client of applicable state or federal law, rule or regulation"; the former breach-of-Agreement, System Agreement, Web Site and product-injury limbs are deleted.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-party claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (i) gives a third-party IP infringement/misappropriation indemnity in favour of Client (element string as supplied concerns the Vendor IP indemnity, which is present).

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no modification exclusion was added, so the condition does not apply and the indemnity is broader (more favourable to Customer) than the fallback allows.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion appears in the inserted text, so the allowance is simply unused and no defect arises.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification exclusion appears, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no procure/modify/replace remedy ladder; it stops at the defend-and-indemnify obligation and the notice/control/cooperation mechanics.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees fallback remedy anywhere in the rendered Section 12.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x super-cap is drafted; the retained cap at p0077 reaches only Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 and therefore does not touch Section 12 (deliberate, and favourable to us).

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (i): "an allegation that the Interface, Hosting Services or Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right", within a third-party-claim indemnity in Client's favour.

reasons: Finding status is correct: Section 12(b) as written covers only TrueLink's breach of the Agreement, with no third-party IP cover, no defence duty and no procedure, and Sections 9/p0076 give no non-infringement warranty — so the clause fails the fallback's first element and is a deviation rather than a clause sitting at the fallback.

The preferred checklist is complete on the operative text: defence duty to Client and affiliates, third-party claim scope, all four indemnified heads (IP infringement of the Interface/Hosting/Support Services, breach of applicable law, TrueLink-caused unauthorised access to Client Content or Credit Data, gross negligence or willful misconduct), and notice / control-of-defence / reasonable-cooperation mechanics, plus a narrowed Client indemnity limited to Client Content and Client's violations of law.

The fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund backstop, no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level; the comment correctly offers the fallback as a negotiation option rather than relying on it in operative text.

Minimal: two surgical operations only — one inserted paragraph and one narrowing of Section 12(a). Existing favourable language is retained (Section 12(b)'s broader breach-of-Agreement indemnity survives and is not duplicated by the new IP/law/data-breach/GNWM heads, and the uncapped position for Section 12 is preserved because the p0077 cap is untouched and reaches only Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11).

Preserves intent: liability cap, fees, term and all other mechanics are unchanged, and no new obligation contradicts the retained text. The only trade is the deliberate narrowing of our own indemnity, which is itself a preferred-level requirement.

Optional refinement (not a defect): the procedure sentence applies to "[e]ach indemnity under this Section 12", which also conditions the pre-existing Section 12(b) indemnity on notice and cedes defence control to TrueLink. Consider limiting the sentence to third-party claims (e.g. "with respect to any third-party claim") and adding "; the indemnifying party may not settle any claim imposing liability or admission on the indemnified party without its consent" so we do not lose ground on first-party claims under 12(b).
